title: Living documentation project classification configuration
description: Optional .living-documentation.json at the project root. It affects classification, check scope, related-document discovery, and the documentation tree; it never relocates project artifacts. This schema is the single source of truth for accepted keys: the bundled scripts read it at run time.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema. Ignored by the scripts.

enforcement.description: Retired; it has no effect, because no bundled script reads it. It set how the Stop-hook gate and the session-start rule of the earlier maintaining-living-documentation skill treated a project, and both were removed with that skill. The key is still accepted so that a configuration written for that skill keeps loading.

exclude_globs.description: Extra paths to skip, in addition to the built-in exclusions. Patterns are matched against project-relative POSIX paths; a leading '**/' also matches at the top level.

specification_globs.description: Files to classify as authoritative specifications or contracts.

decision_globs.description: Files to classify as decision records.

evidence_globs.description: Files to classify as evidence (tests, benchmarks, validation).

generated_globs.description: Files to classify as generated artifacts.

infrastructure_globs.description: Files to classify as infrastructure, deployment, or CI definitions.

configuration_globs.description: Files to classify as configuration, build, or dependency manifests.

max_candidates.description: Most related documents (distinct paths) find_related.py lists; the closest are kept first and the rest are counted in 'truncated'. Advisory comment records are not counted.

min_name_length.description: Shortest file name that counts as a mention of a changed file in a document. Shorter names match only when the whole project-relative path appears.

products.description: Directories that are products: separately built or deployed units inside this repository. Patterns are matched per path segment: '*' stays inside one segment and '**' spans any number of them.

features.description: Directories that are feature folders, matched like products. A directory that matches both products and features is a configuration error.

tree.description: Declares the documentation tree: the repository root is always its root node, every directory that holds a listed file (tracked or untracked, not ignored by Git, not excluded) and matches a pattern is a node of that kind, and each node's parent is the nearest node above it. With this key, check_tree.py requires a README.md in every node that links to each child node and back to its parent; without it, check_tree.py only proposes patterns.
